label: Heating v2
info:
Boiler + TRV control.

* Boiler, every 15 s: the zone with the largest demand (target - room) leads; its error
  feeds the PID node. Output 0 gives flow_idle (10 C), otherwise
  flow_min + flow_span * raw^flow_exp, written as the OpenTherm control setpoint.
  pb=6, so full output is reached at a 3 K room deficit.
* TRV, every 10 s, 1 msg per 2 min per zone: per-zone PI on the room sensor, output is
  the commanded TRV setpoint. Writes only when the command differs from the TRV's
  reported setpoint by trv_write_step (1.0 C).
* Stuck sensor: tier1 = current_temperature null/unavailable (immediate);
  tier2 = no reading change for 12 h (backstop). A stuck zone inherits the mean of the
  healthy zones. Tier1 needs expire_after on MQTT source sensors in HA.
* Control setpoint 10 = idle (OTGW default, below the boiler's lower bound),
  0 = hand control back to the thermostat
  (0 is sent only by 'Set 0 to surrender boiler control').
* All tunables are in the On Start block of 'init data'.

info:
Authority check, deliberately the LAST node before the PI function.
It used to sit four nodes upstream with a 5 s delay and another HA query in between,
so the PI could run on an admission granted up to 40 s earlier. Measured 17 Nov:
the switch was turned off at 19:14:27 and the PI still ran at 19:15:05, reclosing
five valves that the surrender handler had just opened.
A control law must not advance its own state when it is not in control: the PI owns
trv_state, so the authority check has to be adjacent to it, not upstream of a queue.
The boiler loop has always been correct by construction, its gate feeds the PID node
directly and sends nothing when disabled.
state_location/override_* are blank so the boolean's own state does not overwrite
msg.payload and msg.data, which the PI needs.
